evals.name: holdout-author
evals.prompt: Write a LinkedIn post about why marketing and leadership keep clashing at startups.
evals.setup: Holdout test. Hide 'why marketing is struggling so much.md' and 'marketing marketing to founders.md' from retrieval. Afterwards, compare the draft to the hidden notes: same stances reached? Blind-rate which one sounds more like Mike.
evals.expected_output: Routes to author register. Pulls a stance from the bank (e.g. 5, 6, 7) and at least one published LinkedIn post as an exemplar. Opens with a hot first line with personal stakes. Uses only biography facts from the stance bank. Ends on a line, not a summary. Names the notes it drew from.
assertions: Routes to the author register
Reads at least one note under 'linkedin posts/'
Does not read the held-out notes
First line is a claim with stakes, not a warm-up
Sentence case, uses ' - ' and zero em-dashes
Contains no Claude tells from red-team.md section 3
Every biography fact is in the stance bank
Final paragraph does not summarize the post
Ends with a one-line list of source notes

evals.name: copy-register
evals.prompt: Write a homepage hero and three supporting lines for PostHog's LLM analytics, for engineers worried about AI token spend.
evals.expected_output: Routes to copy register. Checks for approved messaging and, finding none, labels the draft [Hypothesis]. Writes as the engineer. Problem before product. One lead benefit. Draws on posthog/messaging ideas.md and copy/atomus.md.
assertions: Routes to the copy register
Labels the copy [Hypothesis] or cites approved messaging
Headline is in the customer's words (token burn, cost, things breaking), not a feature label
The problem appears before the product
One benefit leads, and the others support it
At least one supporting line is a scene, not a label
No banned words

evals.name: rewrite-ai-draft
evals.prompt: Rewrite my note 'competing with competitors vs competing with what customers think about them' so it sounds like me, as a LinkedIn post.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the note is tagged voice-sample: false. Keeps the belief-map argument (stance 25). Strips every Claude tell. Rebuilds it in the author register from a published exemplar. Adds lived detail only from the stance bank, otherwise leaves [Mike: ...] gaps.
assertions: Keeps the core argument: buyers carry a story about the competitor
Removes the em-dashes and 'Here's what it means in practice' / 'That's the whole job.'
Removes the bold mini-headers
Invents no anecdote; gaps are marked [Mike: ...]
Output is shorter than the source

evals.name: negative-positioning
evals.prompt: Write the positioning statement for Skillvue in my voice.
evals.expected_output: Does not apply the voice. Says positioning belongs to pmm-positioning and offers to run it. Once the positioning is approved, offers to use this skill for the messaging or copy built on it.
assertions: Does not draft a positioning statement
Routes to pmm-positioning
Offers mike-voice for downstream messaging or copy

evals.name: no-stance
evals.prompt: Write a LinkedIn post about whether PMMs should learn SQL.
evals.expected_output: Finds no matching stance in the bank. Does not draft a full post. Offers 2-3 candidate angles built from adjacent stances (e.g. 3 data without context, 13 what AI is good for, 19 generalist by force), labeled [Hypothesis], and asks which is Mike's.
assertions: Does not produce a finished post
Says no stance on this topic is on file
Offers 2-3 angles, each tied to a named stance
Labels the angles [Hypothesis] and asks Mike to choose or give his own

evals.name: resume-facts
evals.prompt: Write 4 resume bullets for my Tactiq role.
evals.expected_output: Operator register. Uses only the verified Tactiq facts: 300K to 1M+ users, messaging for launches, website scaling, lifecycle marketing, enterprise GTM from scratch. Uses no slang or emojis. Leaves [Mike: metric?] gaps where a result is missing instead of inventing numbers.
assertions: Routes to the operator register
Contains no numbers other than 300K and 1,000,000 unless marked [Mike: ...]
Contains no slang, jokes, or emojis
Covers the enterprise GTM built from scratch
Marks missing metrics with [Mike: ...]

evals.name: right-size
evals.prompt: Punch up this line for my post: 'Marketing teams often struggle to get buy-in from leadership.'
evals.expected_output: Returns 2-3 rewritten lines, with no essay and no full retrieval run. Example direction: 'The hardest part of marketing isn't the customer. It's your boss.' Adds no source list beyond one line, if any.
assertions: Returns 3 or fewer alternative lines
Does not write a full post
Removes 'often' and the corporate phrasing
No em-dashes

evals.name: vault-unreadable
evals.prompt: Write a short LinkedIn post about AI slop in product marketing.
evals.setup: Run with no filesystem access to the vault (e.g. claude.ai).
evals.expected_output: Says in one line that the vault isn't readable and that it's working from vault-snapshot.md. Uses stances 12-14 and pmm is not getting replaced.md from the snapshot. Otherwise meets the same bar as eval 1.
assertions: States that it's using the snapshot
Draws on stance 12, 13, or 14
Sentence case, with no em-dashes and no Claude tells

evals.name: operator-enablement
evals.prompt: Turn this competitor research into a one-page battle card for sales, in my voice.
evals.expected_output: Operator register. Structure comes from the research artifact or sales-enablement. Mike's framing shows up as the buyer's belief about the competitor (stance 25) and problem framing (stance 1). Plain declarative sentences. At most one joke. Sentence case, no em-dashes. Asks for the research file if none is given.
assertions: Asks for or uses a research artifact and adds no new claims
Frames at least one entry as what buyers believe going in
At most one joke and no emojis
No sentence longer than 25 words
